in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to check if I'm eligible. I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you! It's great to meet you and learn about Alex.

To help determine your eligibility, I have a few more questions:

Are you responsible for Alex? This means either:
- Alex lives with you, or
- You contribute to the cost of looking after Alex at least the same amount as Child Benefit (currently £25.60 per week for the eldest child)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you for confirming that.

Next question: Are you and Alex currently living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you!

One more question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else previously claimed Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

Just one more question: Is Alex in full-time education or registered with a careers service? (This is mainly relevant for older children, but I want to confirm for completeness.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex is only 8, so they're just in primary school - regular school, not anything special.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying! Primary school counts as full-time education, so that's all I needed to know.

Based on the information you've provided, I have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me summarise what you've told me:

- Alex is 8 years old
- Alex lives with you in England
- You are responsible for Alex
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- Alex is in full-time education (primary school)

Let me now provide you with the outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

✅ **Age requirement met**: Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
✅ **Responsibility**: Alex lives with you, so you are considered responsible for them
✅ **Residency**: You and Alex both live in the UK (England)
✅ **No duplicate claims**: No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex
✅ **Education**: Alex is in full-time education (primary school)

**Next steps:**
You can apply for Child Benefit online through the official government website, or by post using the Child Benefit claim form (CH2). If Alex was born in the UK, you may have already received this form after registering the birth.

**Please note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through the High Income Child Benefit Charge. However, it can still be worth claiming to protect your National Insurance record and to ensure your child gets their National Insurance number automatically at 16.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
